newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN 10-YR OLO/BUND YLD SPREAD DIPS TO NEW LOW.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN 10-YR OLO/BUND YLD SPREAD DIPS TO NEW LOW.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds ended flat on Friday after initial gains that followed U.S. producer price and retail sales data were eroded later in the afternoon.

However OLOs still managed to outperform Bunds, with the ten year yield premium over equivalent German paper narrowing during the session to a record low of 4.5 basis points, dealers said. It finished at six bp, down from eight on Thursday.

"It has been an up-and-down day, and now we're back where we started," one dealer said, adding he felt uncomfortable with the spread at current levels which he saw at the bottom of a five to ten basis point range.
"A lack of sellers in our market has caused the spread to go down this far," the dealer added. "Personally I'd be happier if we went back to 20 basis points."
The benchmark 2006 OLO ended with a yield of 6.08 percent, down just one basis point from Thursday's close.

December bond futures closed 0.05 lower at 119.45 after initially rallying to 119.73 on news U.S. September PPI rose 0.2 percent, less than the 0.3 percent expected. September retail sale rose more than expected but August's figure was revised downwards.
